author: Contributor 89
about: Tinybird's published examples (its API reference pages, spec/doc-examples.json), each sent as its page sends it, with only the setup its precondition needs. URL import examples use a reader-supplied CSV held by the World application stand-in at the published placeholder URL; the example states no specific source bytes. Every read-back asserts those supplied bytes. Client library render computations have no served HTTP operation and remain unserved published examples.

Neither the demanded applications nor the life uses that flow; they send files, schemas and Events API data. Its published setup creates a connection with POST /v0/connectors, outside those flows. Sources: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/datasource-api and https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/connections-api.

notReplayed.datasource_create_from_definition#doc Mo: The example promises modification of an existing stocks Data Source but POSTs the collection /v0/datasources with mode=create (the default). The vendor’s Data Sources reference instead documents modifications at POST /v0/datasources/(.+)/alter: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/datasource-api#post--v0-datasources-(.+)-alter. The vendor’s API overview states “Pipe, Data Source and node names are globally unique”: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference#naming. Thus creating another stocks cannot perform the promised in-place modification. Both vendor statements contradict the published request’s promised effect; the alteration flow has no demand or life call. The original request is preserved in spec/doc-examples.json.

notReplayed.create_token#doc Creating a new JWT Toke: JWT issuance with expiration_time is a separate authentication flow behind token creation. Neither demand nor life uses JWTs; both use static Workspace tokens. Source: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/token-api.
notReplayed.query_2#doc POST /v0/sql: The page's JSON body is not JSON: its q string holds the template's quotes unescaped ({{String(column_name, "column_name_value")}} inside "q":"…"), so the body ends its string early and no parser reads the fields the page means. Sent as published it is a malformed body, not the example's query; its form-encoded twin on the same page (Running sql queries against your data (2)) is replayed. Source: https://www.tinybird.co/docs/api-reference/query-api.
